summary: UBC's International Scholars Program gives need- and merit-based awards to international students entering a first undergraduate degree straight from secondary school. The awards (Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow, Donald A. Wehrung, International Impact, Vantage One Excellence) can cover up to the full cost of study and living. Winners have top grades (all As or equivalent), real leadership and community impact, and a family that truly cannot pay for UBC.
lookfor: Superior academic achievement (all As or equivalent)
Leadership and exceptional contribution to your school or community
Character and educational goals, shown in four short essays and a video interview
Significant, documented financial need—without help you could not attend UBC
A school nomination and a teacher reference that confirm the above
cycle: For September 2027: award application opened 5 Oct 2026; nomination and teacher reference due a few days before, and your application by, 15 Nov 2026 (11:59 pm Pacific); UBC admission application by 15 Jan 2027; documents to UBC by 31 Jan 2027; video interviews Jan–Mar; decisions Feb–Apr 2027.

eligibility.q: Are you an international student who will need a Canadian study permit?
eligibility.no: Canadian citizens and permanent residents use different UBC awards (e.g. Presidential Scholars, deadline 1 Dec).

eligibility.q: Did you (or will you) graduate from secondary school no earlier than June 2026, and will this be your first undergraduate degree?
eligibility.no: If you already started university or finished school before June 2026, you cannot apply; look at UBC's other international awards or master's funding later.

eligibility.q: Are your grades all As or equivalent (e.g. mostly A1s in WAEC and top school results)?
eligibility.no: Consider UBC merit awards or the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at UBC if your grades are strong but not top.

eligibility.q: Would it be impossible for your family to pay for UBC without major help, and do you have no other external funding?
eligibility.no: If your family can pay part, apply to UBC normally and check its merit-based entrance awards instead (you cannot be considered for merit awards if you apply to this program).

eligibility.q: Can your school counsellor, principal or administrator nominate you, and can a different teacher act as referee?
eligibility.no: A non-profit that runs education or leadership programmes for disadvantaged graduates may nominate you; ask now.

eligibility.q: Is your chosen degree eligible (not Nursing, Dental Hygiene, Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor+Master of Management, or dual/joint degrees)?
eligibility.no: Choose another degree; these are excluded.

steps.title: Check you qualify and choose your degree and campus
steps.why: The award is tied to your UBC admission choice, and some degrees are excluded.
do: Read the International Scholars page from top to bottom.
Use the UBC requirements tool: choose campus (Vancouver or Okanagan), select your country (e.g. Nigeria) and your degree to see the subjects and grades you need.
Choose your degree and campus; note that a school may nominate up to 2 students for Vancouver and 1 for Okanagan.
Use UBC's cost estimator to understand the full cost you are asking for.
tips: Pick the degree that best matches the activities you will write about—it makes your story consistent.
avoid: Choosing an excluded degree such as Nursing.
check: I meet the degree-specific subject requirements.

steps.title: Ask your school for a nomination and a teacher referee
steps.why: Without a nomination you cannot apply, and nominators must submit their form days before 15 November.
do: Book a meeting with your guidance counsellor or principal this week.
Bring a one-page summary: grades, leadership roles, community work, and why you need financial aid.
Ask a different teacher who knows your work in your chosen subject to be your referee.
Collect both people's official email addresses.
Tell them UBC will email them a form, and agree they will submit it by 10 November.
tips: If your school has no counsellor, the principal or a senior administrator can nominate.
avoid: Using the same person as nominator and referee—UBC requires two different people.
check: My nominator and referee have both agreed and I have their emails.

steps.title: Submit your UBC admission application first
steps.why: You must complete your UBC admission application before you can start the award application.
do: Go to UBC's 'Apply now' page; it sends you to EducationPlannerBC, where you create an account and start the UBC application for 2027/28.
Fill in personal details, school history and degree choice(s).
Write the Personal Profile (see next step) and add your two Personal Profile referees.
Pay the CAD 173.25 application fee by card (ask a parent or sponsor with an international card if needed).
Submit and note your UBC application/student number.
tips: The admission deadline is 15 January, but for this award you need it done by early November.
avoid: Waiting for the January deadline—you will miss the 15 November award deadline.
check: I have my UBC application number and a submission confirmation.

steps.title: Write your UBC Personal Profile
steps.why: UBC scores your profile on engagement, leadership, substance and voice; it also feeds your scholarship story.
do: Answer: who you are and how others describe you; what is important to you and why.
List up to five activities or accomplishments (clubs, work, volunteering, sport, family responsibilities).
Pick one or two activities and explain what you did and what you learned.
Use the Additional information box to explain anything unusual (e.g. school strikes, COVID gaps).
Keep each answer within its character limit (roughly 500–2,100 characters); longer text is cut off.
tips: Reflect: say what changed in you, not just what you did.
Family duties (caring for siblings, helping in a family business) count as activities.
avoid: Writing what you think UBC wants instead of your own voice.
check: Each answer has one specific story and one lesson.

steps.prompt: Tell us about who you are; what is important to you and why; your activities; one or two activities in depth.
steps.limit: About 500–2,100 characters per question (shown in the form)

steps.title: Open the award application and send requests
steps.why: The nomination and recommendation forms are only sent when you request them inside the portal.
do: Open the 2027 International Scholars Program application portal and create an account.
Set your time zone to Pacific Time in the settings.
Under Tasks, request the nomination (enter your nominator) and the recommendation (enter your teacher).
Mark all ubc.ca email addresses as safe so replies do not go to spam.
tips: Send the requests the same day you open the account; your referees need time.
avoid: Typing a wrong email—the form will never arrive.
check: Both tasks show 'requested' in the portal.

steps.title: Gather your family's financial information
steps.why: Financial need is assessed in detail; vague or missing figures weaken your case.
do: Sit with your parents/guardians and list annual family income from all sources.
List annual expenses, assets (land, house, vehicles, savings) and debts.
List dependants and the school fees paid for each.
Collect official proof the portal asks for (e.g. pay slips, employer letters, tax or business records).
Convert amounts carefully (e.g. naira to Canadian dollars) and state the rate you used.
tips: If a parent is a farmer or trader without pay slips, a signed letter from a community leader or local government office describing income can help—explain it in the form.
avoid: Hiding assets or guessing figures; inconsistencies hurt trust.
check: Income, expenses and assets add up and match the documents.

steps.title: Write the four award essays
steps.why: The essays are where selectors judge leadership, community impact and goals.
do: Open the application form in the portal and copy the four questions into a document.
Plan each answer: one specific situation, what you did, the result, and what you learned.
Write about 150–250 words per essay (check each box's limit in the form).
Use different examples in each essay; avoid repeating your Personal Profile word for word.
Ask a teacher to check clarity and grammar.
tips: Show impact with numbers: 'tutored 30 juniors; 22 passed WAEC maths'.
For the International Impact Award, link your work to sustainability, social justice or health.
avoid: Starting late—UBC says late-started applications are less likely to succeed.
check: Each essay has a clear example and result.
steps.prompt: Four questions in the award form on leadership, community contribution, character and goals (see portal).

steps.title: Make sure nominator and referee submit
steps.why: Your application is incomplete if their forms are missing at the deadline.
do: Check the portal tasks list weekly.
Give your nominator and teacher a short reminder sheet: your achievements, activities and goals.
Remind them politely by 8 November if the status has not changed.
Thank them once submitted.
tips: Offer to print the email or sit with them while they open the link if they are not used to online forms.
avoid: Assuming they have submitted without checking the portal.

steps.title: Complete and submit the award application
steps.why: The 15 November deadline (11:59 pm Pacific) is about 8:59 am on 16 November in Nigeria (WAT)—but do not cut it close.
do: Fill in the activities and awards sections with dates and your role.
Enter financial information and upload documents.
Paste the final essays and proofread.
Check every task is marked complete.
Submit by 12 November and save the confirmation.
tips: Ask someone to read the whole application once for consistency.
avoid: Network or power failure on deadline day; submit early.

steps.title: Send academic documents to UBC admissions
steps.why: The program page says admission documents are due by 31 January 2027.
do: Log in to your UBC applicant account and check the documents list.
Upload or arrange your school transcripts and certificates (WAEC/NECO results as asked).
Submit English test results if UBC says you need them.
Send anything else UBC admissions requests.
tips: If your WAEC result is not released yet, upload predicted/interim results as UBC instructs and follow up.

WAEC/WASSCE English is not listed as meeting UBC's English Language Admission Standard. Check the list of accepted pathways; if none fits, book IELTS, TOEFL, PTE or Duolingo early (English proof is due by 15 February 2027).
avoid: Ignoring document requests while waiting for the award.
Assuming you are exempt from English proof because your school taught in English—check the official list.
check: My applicant account shows no missing documents.

steps.title: Record the video interview if invited
steps.why: Shortlisted applicants record video answers between January and March and have one week to finish.
do: Check your email and spam daily from January.
Practise answering out loud: your leadership story, a challenge you overcame, why UBC, your plans after university.
Find a quiet, well-lit room and stable internet.
Record your answers in the portal within the one-week window.
tips: Speak to the camera, not your notes; keep each answer to its time limit.
avoid: Opening the invitation on the last day of the week.
check: I have recorded and submitted all responses.

steps.title: Get the decision and plan your study permit
steps.why: Decisions come between February and April; the study permit takes time.
do: Watch for the award decision (Feb–Apr 2027).
If you win, accept the award and admission offer.
Apply for your Canadian study permit using your offer and award letters.
Apply for UBC housing after the award decision (housing deadline 1 May 2027).
tips: Scholars get dedicated advising and workshops—join them from day one.
avoid: Applying for housing before you know your award; UBC advises waiting.
check: I know my result and next deadline.

faq.q: Do I choose which award (McKellin, Wehrung, Impact, Vantage One)?
faq.a: No. You are automatically considered for every award you are eligible for.

faq.q: Can I also get UBC merit entrance scholarships?
faq.a: No. If you apply to the International Scholars Program you cannot be considered for UBC's merit-based awards.

faq.q: I finished secondary school in 2025. Can I apply?
faq.a: No. For 2027 entry you must have graduated no earlier than June 2026.

faq.q: My school has no counsellor. Who nominates me?
faq.a: Your principal or another school administrator, or an eligible non-profit education organisation.

faq.q: Is there an application fee for the award?
faq.a: The award application itself has no stated fee, but the UBC admission application costs CAD 173.25 for international applicants.

faq.q: Does my WAEC English count as English proof?
faq.a: It is not listed among UBC's accepted options. Check the English Language Admission Standard page and plan to take an accepted test such as IELTS, TOEFL or Duolingo.
